title: StrataForge integration pipeline and packaging sync

Discussed Helm/operator approach, image signing, KMS/HSM integration, VPC peering options, and minimal footprint benchmarks. Agreed to produce a joint README, checklist for marketplace compliance, and a small lab deployment to validate SLOs.

Samira Khan: Confirm KMS/HSM vendor and cert matrix, include SOC2 report if available (due: 2027-08-24)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-16 11:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya T., Carlos R., Priya N., Lina P., Arjun P., Samira K., Devon L.
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated): packaging and infra sync, action items captured.

00:00 Maya Thompson: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through how we think about the packaging pipeline for the marketplace listing and also the hybrid deployment pattern, does that sound right?
00:18 Lina Park: yeah that's perfect — main goal is we need a reproducible deploy flow for both our managed offering and onprem installs, and some checklist for marketplace.
00:27 Carlos Ruiz: quick note, i think we should separate two tracks: 1) listing/marketplace compliance (billing, metering, images) and 2) runtime operator/helm packaging for customers. they overlap but have different owners.
00:42 Arjun Patel: yep, for us platform needs the operator route because we manage upgrades across clusters, helm is fine but operator gives CRD lifecycle.
00:53 Maya Thompson: noted. Priya, you had some thoughts on operator vs helm?
01:02 Priya Nair: yeah, we've done both. operator gives more control and can manage KV cache warming and partitioned routing, but adds complexity. helm is faster to onboard for marketplace. we usually provide both: a helm chart for quick install and a lightweight operator for enterprise deployments.
01:22 Devon Lee: question — how opinionated is Redwood's private control plane? e.g., do we need a peered VPC or will an agent outbound to your control plane suffice?
01:34 Carlos Ruiz: good question. for Private deployments we support both patterns: outbound agent mode (customer egress to Redwood control plane) and VPC peering with a private control plane. peered VPC needs IP allow lists, BGP is not required.
01:53 Samira Khan: from security we need KMS integration and image signing. we can't accept unsigned container images.
02:02 Maya Thompson: understood. we have documented support for customer KMS via KMS providers and HSMs; image signing can be integrated into the pipeline — we can show an example with cosign or sigstore.
02:15 Lina Park: perfect. can you put an example repo link?
02:19 Maya Thompson: yes i'll share the repo after the call — we'll include a cosign example and minimal CI.
02:25 Arjun Patel: networking wise we'll need a sample firewall list. for peering what's the port list?
02:32 Carlos Ruiz: minimal ports are for gRPC control plane on 8443, telemetry on 4317, and registry pull HTTPS 443. we'll send a hardened list.
02:45 Devon Lee: do you have an operator image that's quantum-optimized — i mean small? our infra is tight on node memory.
02:53 Priya Nair: we try to keep the operator footprint <200MB compressed. runtime images are bigger of course. also we recommend quantized model images for edge.
03:05 Lina Park: can we talk about the marketplace packaging? billing hooks are required right? metering?
03:12 Maya Thompson: yes the marketplace expects a licensing integration for metering. Redwood's marketplace package includes a metering sidecar that emits usage events to the marketplace billing endpoint; we can make that optional for onprem.
03:25 Arjun Patel: about telemetry — we need to control PII. can telemetry be scrubbed or routed to our splunk?
03:33 Carlos Ruiz: telemetry supports masking and can be configured to ship to customer endpoints via OTLP. we also support local-only telemetry (no outbound) when using private control plane.
03:45 Lina Park: great. any SSO requirements for the listing? we use Okta and want SAML SSO into the console.
03:51 Maya Thompson: we support SAML/OIDC SSO; for marketplace listing you still need a service account for the listing flows but user-facing SSO is fine.
04:02 Samira Khan: for compliance can you provide your SOC2 cert and encryption in transit diagram?
04:08 Maya Thompson: yes i'll attach our latest SOC2 and an architecture diagram.
04:14 Carlos Ruiz: back to operator vs helm — from an upgrade perspective operator can orchestrate model rollouts and cache invalidation across nodes which helm can't easily do without ad hoc scripts.
04:30 Arjun Patel: would the operator handle KV cache pre-warming? we often have cold-start latency concerns.
04:37 Priya Nair: operator exposes a cache-warm CRD, you can define prefixes to prepopulate KV cache and warm shards. we saw 30-40% improvement in cold-start in our internal tests.
04:50 Devon Lee: that's encouraging. what's the recommended GPU sizing for 2 concurrent streams at 2k tokens?
04:57 Carlos Ruiz: for a standard decoder model with 16k context that's roughly 1 A100 per 8 concurrent low-latency streams; for 2k tokens you could pack more, but benchmark script will clarify. we'll produce a reference config.
05:10 Lina Park: can we get a short lab run to validate latency SLOs for our use case?
05:15 Maya Thompson: yes we'll set up a 1-week sandbox with 2 GPU nodes and run the benchmark.
05:21 Arjun Patel: what about quantization/heterogeneous GPU mixes? we have some older T4s in edge sites.
05:28 Priya Nair: runtime supports quantized variants and model routing can fallback to smaller quantized model. but that requires model variants to be included in the image repo.
05:40 Samira Khan: on encryption, does Redwood require customer keys to be in KMS or can we use an HSM onsite?
05:47 Carlos Ruiz: both supported. we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs via PKCS11. note: HSM integration will need additional cert exchange.
05:58 Devon Lee: about the listing manifest — which files are required?
06:02 Maya Thompson: we'll provide a checklist but typically: manifest.yaml, license terms, a helm chart (or operator bundle), vendor logo, support contact, and a lightweight quickstart. also a security.yaml with the threat model and data flow.
06:20 Lina Park: ok, on the marketplace side our product manager wants to know how long the listing certification takes.
06:27 Maya Thompson: certification for us is 2-3 weeks once we hand in artifacts; marketplace review by partner teams can add additional time.
06:34 Arjun Patel: any blockers for us? we heard some partners had trouble with container scanning.
06:38 Carlos Ruiz: we integrate with scanning partners and can provide attestation files. if your pipeline already has SCA and SBOM that's ideal.
06:47 Samira Khan: about audit logs — can we retain logs for 7 years per our policy?
06:53 Maya Thompson: logs retention in Redwood Console can be extended with enterprise add-on; for Private you control retention locally. we'll add that note to checklist.
07:05 Lina Park: do you have a template Network diagram for peering?
07:09 Carlos Ruiz: yes, i'll attach a sample with IP ranges and NAT details.
07:15 Devon Lee: will the Helm chart support kustomize overlays? we use overlays for staging vs prod.
07:21 Priya Nair: we recommend making the chart patchable via values and providing a kustomize example.
07:28 Arjun Patel: on upgrades if we use the operator can we do canary model deploys?
07:33 Carlos Ruiz: yes operator supports canary rollouts with traffic splitting. it ties into routing policy — you can route by token, by route or by percent.
07:45 Lina Park: for data residency, some EU customers require models to run in-region. does your private control plane support region pinning?
07:52 Maya Thompson: yes, deployment profiles allow region pinning; routing policy can keep inference in-region.
07:58 Samira Khan: any third-party dependencies we should flag?
08:02 Priya Nair: container registry, S3-compatible storage for model artifacts, and optionally an external metrics backend.
08:10 Devon Lee: ok. can we record a short dev walk-through video for our onboarding docs?
08:14 Maya Thompson: yes will do — we'll record a 10-min demo.
08:17 Arjun Patel: what's the proposed timeline for a PoC?
08:20 Maya Thompson: propose: packaging checklist and repo by 2027-08-20; lab benchmark week of 2027-08-23; security artifact exchange by 2027-08-24; initial PoC sign-off by 2027-08-31.
08:32 Lina Park: sounds good.
08:35 Carlos Ruiz: any other technical red flags?
08:38 Samira Khan: none so far, just the KMS certs to verify.
08:42 Maya Thompson: great. I'll summarize and share actions. thanks everyone.
08:47 Devon Lee: thanks all.
